name: Pyrolysis oil and hydrothermal liquefaction
principle: Fast pyrolysis heats biomass to about 500 degC with short residence time to give up to 65 wt% liquid; hydrothermal liquefaction (HTL) converts wet feeds in water at about 250 to 370 degC and 4 to 20 MPa to a bio-crude. Both oils are oxygen-rich and need upgrading by hydrodeoxygenation or co-processing. ETIP rates pyrolysis at TRL 8, HTL pilots at TRL 5.

process_steps.name: Biomass preparation (drying for pyrolysis; slurry for HTL)
Fast pyrolysis reactor or HTL reactor

suppliers.name: Ensyn
suppliers.product: fast pyrolysis (RTP), plants in North America

performance.metric: liquid yield from fast pyrolysis (dry basis)
performance.basis: at about 500 degC; bio-oil has about half the energy content of fuel oil, 35 to 40% oxygen, pH below 2

source.note: ETIP Bioenergy, Transport fuels via pyrolytic and thermolytic conversion
IEA ETP Clean Energy Technology Guide, dataset of 24 July 2026, latest assessment (IEA 1-11 scale): 'Biomass pyrolysis' 7 (2025); 'Hydrothermal liquefaction and upgrading of biomass' 6 (2025)

advantages: Wet feeds can go to HTL without drying
limitations: Bio-oil acidity and oxygen need upgrading; HTL pumping of slurries is hard on equipment
